title: Tensor and sheafification for modules over a presheaf of rings
statement: Let $(\mathcal C,J)$ be a site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], let $\mathcal O$ be a presheaf [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] of commutative rings, and let $\mathcal F,\mathcal G$ be presheaves [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification] of $\mathcal O$-modules. Let $\mathcal F\otimes_{p,\mathcal O}\mathcal G$ be the presheaf of $\mathcal O$-modules $U\mapsto\mathcal F(U)\otimes_{\mathcal O(U)}\mathcal G(U)$, with restriction maps induced by those of $\mathcal F$, $\mathcal G$ and $\mathcal O$, and let $\mathcal F^\#$, $\mathcal G^\#$, $(\mathcal F\otimes_{p,\mathcal O}\mathcal G)^\#$ be the module sheafifications, sheaves of $\mathcal O^\#$-modules [lem-pc-sites-module-sheafification-interface]. There is a canonical isomorphism of sheaves of $\mathcal O^\#$-modules $\mathcal F^\#\otimes_{\mathcal O^\#}\mathcal G^\#\cong(\mathcal F\otimes_{p,\mathcal O}\mathcal G)^\#$ [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], natural in $\mathcal F$ and $\mathcal G$. In particular, if $\mathcal G$ is a sheaf of $\mathcal O^\#$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] and $\iota\mathcal G$ denotes $\mathcal G$ regarded as a presheaf of $\mathcal O$-modules by restriction of scalars along $\mathcal O\to\mathcal O^\#$, then for every presheaf $\mathcal F$ of $\mathcal O$-modules there is an isomorphism $\mathcal G\otimes_{\mathcal O^\#}\mathcal F^\#\cong(\iota\mathcal G\otimes_{p,\mathcal O}\mathcal F)^\#$, natural in $\mathcal G$ and $\mathcal F$.

proof.text: Construct tensorSheafificationUnits sectionwise by ModuleCat.MonoidalCategory.tensorLift on the two sheafification units. Additivity and scalar compatibility follow from linearity of the units and the tensor relations. Naturality follows from PresheafOfModules.naturality_apply. This is a genuine construction with no postponed data.

Use sheafificationHomEquiv to extend tensorSheafificationUnits followed by the ring-sheaf module sheafification unit. Compose with tensorObjIsoSheafification.inv to obtain sheafificationTensorComparisonApp. comparisonApp_unit follows from Equiv.apply_symm_apply; evaluation on pure tensors gives comparisonApp_tmul. The adjunction equivalence and sectionwise tensor extensionality give sheafifiedTensor_hom_ext.

For tensorSheaf_hom_ext, curry the maps obtained by precomposition with the pure-tensor pairing. Uniqueness in existsUnique_bilinear_sheafification_extension identifies the two extended bilinear families from equality on the original presheaf factors. Uniqueness in tensor_bilinear_universal then identifies the two sheaf tensor morphisms.

Apply bilinear extension to the tensor pairing of the unit at F tensor G, with target its sheafification. Apply tensor_bilinear_universal to obtain the inverse morphism phi. Its original-section characterization is hphi. For comparison followed by phi, sheafifiedTensor_hom_ext reduces the identity to comparisonApp_tmul and hphi. For phi followed by comparison, tensorSheaf_hom_ext reduces it to the same two formulas. This proves comparisonApp_isIso without choosing any data from a mere unproved existence theorem.

Naturality of tensorObjIsoSheafification follows by composing the source library whiskerLeft_tensorObjIsoSheafification_hom and whiskerRight_tensorObjIsoSheafification_hom lemmas. Naturality of the ring-sheafification unit gives tensorPure_natural. The two original unit naturality equations, evaluated on pure tensors, give tensorUnits_natural. Apply sheafificationHomEquiv.injective and combine these equations with comparisonApp_unit to prove comparisonApp_natural. Package the components into a natural transformation c; componentwise invertibility gives IsIso c. Its inverse natural isomorphism is the requested e, and comparisonApp_tmul supplies the specified pure-tensor identity.

For the sheaf-factor specialization let B be forget followed by restrictScalars and S be sheafification. Mathlib already proves the counit B composed with S to the identity invertible (via the underlying abelian sheafification counit). Tensor the inverse counit with the identity of S using NatIso.prod and whisker by tensor, then compose with the first comparison whiskered by B.prod identity. This gives exactly the stated bifunctor isomorphism.
